critique.good: Column 1 is wide enough that most compounds need only one or two lines, and the abbreviation column stays on one line. There is no horizontal scroll.
critique.problems: The explanations are squeezed into a very narrow column, producing 5–6-line paragraphs and 153px rows. Columns 1–2 sit mostly empty beside tall prose, so the table feels unbalanced and grows to 906px. The longest compounds still break inside the word.
critique.cause: Column 3 is only 237px (216px text), which forces excessive wrapping, while column 1 at 360px over-allocates space to identifiers and still falls short of the 546px longest term. Column 2 is already at its 122px one-line minimum.

critique.good: Much more compact at 580px; explanations read comfortably at 377px and rows stay at 83–106px. No horizontal scroll.
critique.problems: The primary identifiers in column 1 are broken into three or four mid-word fragments, making the compounds hard to recognise and compare. The short-form column is relatively generous while the term column is starved, so the identifier pair looks distorted.
critique.cause: Column 1 at 220px gives only 199px of text, far below the ~294px needed to hold the 546px longest term in two lines. Column 2 remains at 122px even though its longest cell needs only 101px, so the saved width went to prose rather than to the term column.

critique.good: Every cell is on one line, rows are compact, and column roles are clear. No mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The table is 1802px wide and overflows the 720px frame by 1082px. The explanation column is pushed off-screen, so readers must scroll horizontally and lose the row context. It solves wrapping by abandoning the page.
critique.cause: Column 1 is sized to 567px for the 546px term and column 3 to 1112px for the 1091px one-line explanation, making the total far wider than the available 719px.

critique.good: The most balanced of the two: Kurzform at 122px keeps every abbreviation, including Kfz-Haftpflicht, on one line; Erklärung at 301px gives the prose a usable measure; and the table avoids one-letter orphans.
critique.problems: Begriff at 296px (275px of text) is too narrow for the 546px compound: row 3 breaks as '...überwachun / gsaufgaben...' and row 4 leaves a single 'g' alone on a third line. The table is tall because those header cells and the 4–5-line explanations compete for height.
critique.cause: Column 1 is narrower than the longest compound, so the browser splits inside the word. Column 2 is correctly sized for its 101px one-line content, so the only real trade-off is column 1 versus column 3.

critique.good: Erklärung at 315px is the more comfortable prose measure and the table is slightly shorter (720px vs 743px); abbreviations still fit on one line.
critique.problems: Begriff at 282px is visibly too narrow: 'Donau...gesellschaft' leaves 't' alone and 'Bundes...gesetz' leaves 'z' alone; rows 3 and 4 split even more awkwardly. These orphan letters damage the row headers, which are the main scanning key.
critique.cause: Width was shifted from column 1 to column 3, leaving column 1 with only 261px of text. Column 2 cannot give up much width without breaking Kfz-Haftpflicht, so this is a direct column 1/column 3 allocation error.

critique.good: Best of the three. No overflow, headers stay on one line, and col 1 at 306px gives relatively clean break points for the two very long compounds. Col 2 at 122px keeps Kfz-Haftpflicht intact. The table reads as a coherent glossary.
critique.problems: Col 2 still looks wide and empty for short abbreviations such as DDG and SÜG. Several explanation cells run to 5 lines, making the table 743px tall. Col 1 still splits the two longest compounds, but that is unavoidable at 720px.
critique.cause: Col 2 is sized to the one-line width of Kfz-Haftpflicht/header (101px + 21px), leaving only 291px for Erklärung. Col 1 cannot reach the 546px needed to keep the longest term intact, so prose pays the price.

critique.good: Col 1 gets more room for the compound terms, col 2 stays intact, and there is no horizontal overflow.
critique.problems: The table is taller (766px) and the explanation column feels cramped at 277px. The extra 14px in col 1 does not make any long compound intact, and it shifts the break positions in rows 3–4 to less pleasant places.
critique.cause: Width was moved from Erklärung to Begriff, but col 1 at 320px is still far below the 546px needed for the longest term. The result adds prose wrapping without solving the compound problem.

critique.good: All compound terms fit intact on one line, the table is much shorter (534px), and row heights drop. It is a useful demonstration of what preserving col 1 costs.
critique.problems: The table overflows the 720px box by 370px, so the explanation column is clipped and the reader must scroll horizontally. Because rows are read left-to-right as units, losing the explanation beside the identifier is a serious usability failure. Col 2 is still wide.
critique.cause: Keeping col 1 at 567px (546px text + padding) plus col 2 at 122px leaves 400px for Erklärung, producing a 1090px table. The intact-compound goal forces overflow well beyond the available width.

understanding.purpose: A German glossary/reference table for very long compound terms, pairing each term with its abbreviation and a plain-language explanation.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a row by scanning the full compound term or its short form, then read the explanation. Comparison happens mainly within a row, not across numeric columns.
groups: Columns 1–2 form the identifier pair: the full compound and its abbreviation name the same entity and should stay adjacent and visually linked.
Column 3 is supporting prose, subordinate to the identifier pair and read after it.
keep_intact: Abbreviations in column 2, especially hyphenated forms such as Kfz-Haftpflicht
The 186px unbreakable word in column 3 if possible
Compound terms in column 1 where width allows; split only when necessary
may_wrap: Long compound terms in column 1 when the chosen width cannot hold them

bad.why: The first column is only 220px (199px text), far below the 546px longest term, so the table's key compounds are chopped into 3–4 short fragments; the row headers become hard to scan and compare.
The table is 1802px wide and overflows the 720px box by 1082px; explanation lines run to 1091px, so the reader loses row context and must scroll excessively to compare anything.
The 296px first column leaves a one-letter orphan in the longest compound ('...verordnun/g') and splits key terms awkwardly; the 5-line rows are a symptom of misallocated width.
The 282px first column produces one-letter orphans ('...gesellschaf/t', '...geset/z') in the row-identifying column, which is visually unacceptable.

final.rationale: This table is about long compounds, so the first column is the primary object: at 567px it keeps the longest term intact, and 122px keeps the short forms on one line. r2C accepts a 370px horizontal scroll, but the Kurzform column remains visible as a row anchor when the reader scrolls to the explanation, so rows still read as units. The 400px explanation column gives a readable 3–4-line measure instead of r0C's 1091px single lines. r3A is the best fully fitting compromise, but it still breaks the longest compounds mid-word.

general: When a column contains the table's subject as unbreakable identifiers, protect its longest token before allocating prose width; horizontal scroll can be less damaging than shredding the identifiers.
A short-code column can act as a row anchor during horizontal scroll; size it to its longest token and keep it adjacent to the prose.
Prose columns need a readable measure; avoiding wrapping by making prose 1000px wide trades row height for unreadable line length.
Column widths should reflect content roles, not symmetry: identifiers, codes, and prose need different minima.
specific: Here the first column needs 567px to keep the longest German compound intact; at 720px total, that forces either mid-word breaks or overflow.
The Kurzform column only needs about 122px; giving it more steals width from the explanation.
The best no-scroll designs still break 'Grundstücksverkehrsgenehmigungszuständigkeits...' awkwardly after 'zu'.
r0C's 1802px width is not justified by the content; 400px is enough for the explanations.

final.tradeoffs: Fit versus intact words: 720px cannot satisfy both. r2C chooses integrity and a 370px scroll; r3A chooses fit and accepts compound breaks. A reader who values seeing all three columns at once may prefer r3A, while one who values the compounds as data will prefer r2C.
final.uncertain: Whether 370px of horizontal scroll is acceptable in the intended publication context; whether the Kurzform column is reliably visible during scrolling; and whether breaks at German compound boundaries are acceptable without visible hyphens.

A.why: Everything fits on screen with a sensible three-way balance and readable row rhythm, but the compound-word column is squeezed to ~305px so it breaks the very terms the table is about mid-morpheme ('...überwachung / saufgabenübertragungsgesetz'), and the explanation column at ~232px wraps into many short lines, making rows tall and the text choppy.

B.why: The Begriff column (~555px) keeps every compound intact, which suits the topic, but the Erklärung column is pushed almost entirely outside the 720px box — only fragments ('Gese…', 'Dona…') are visible, so the table's actual content requires horizontal scrolling to read at all.

C.why: Best compromise: all three columns visible, the explanation column gets the most width of the no-scroll layouts (~245px) and wraps in comfortable phrase-length lines, Kurzform is snug but only breaks at a legitimate hyphen ('Kfz-/Haftpflicht'), and the Begriff column is as wide as the budget allows (~310px) so only the two longest compounds split.

D.why: A very wide Begriff column (~530px) leaves most cells half-empty, while the explanation column is clipped off the right edge and unreadable; the wasted white space and hidden content are both unjustified.

E.why: Begriff is cut to ~225px, so nearly every compound is shattered into arbitrary fragments ('...gesell / schaft', '...förderung / sgesetz'), which defeats the table's purpose, and Kurzform is tight enough to feel cramped.

F.why: Explanation column is the most readable of the all-visible layouts (~295px, few lines, no splits), but this is bought by narrowing Begriff to ~290px, which breaks compounds mid-word ('...fahrtsge / sellschaft', '...förderu / ngsgesetz') and leaves those identifiers hard to recognise.

reviews.unsure: Exact pixel widths read off the screenshots; whether horizontal scrolling (B/D) is considered acceptable by the publication, which would change how harshly those are judged.

A.why: Balanced three-column rhythm: Begriff ~293px, Kurzform ~96px, Erklärung ~324px. The explanation wraps to 4–6 comfortable lines, and the huge compound splits into two substantial halves rather than slivers. Small blemish: 'Kfz-Haftpflicht' breaks into 'Kfz-' / 'Haftpflicht' although the short-form column has spare room.

B.why: Begriff is given ~543px (nearly the whole box) and the Erklärung column is squeezed to ~70px and pushed past the dashed frame, so the explanatory text is cut off mid-word and requires horizontal scrolling to read at all. The table's primary content is effectively hidden while col 1's whitespace dominates.

C.why: Essentially the A solution refined: Begriff ~290px, Kurzform ~99px, Erklärung ~321px. Explanation reads in 4–6 lines, the long compounds break at sensible mid-points, and 'Kfz-Haftpflicht' stays whole on one line. Good hierarchy and proportion with no clipped content.

D.why: Erklärung is generously wide (~400px) and very readable, but Begriff is starved at ~220px: 'Donau…fahrtsge/sellschaft', 'Bundesausbildungsförderu/ngsgesetz', '…übertragu/ngsgesetz' leave 2–9 letter orphan fragments, mangling the very identifiers the table is about. Row headers no longer scan as units.

E.why: Same failure mode as B: a ~540px Begriff column plus ~113px Kurzform leaves the Erklärung column ~60px and clipped by the dashed box edge. Every explanation line is truncated; the reader must scroll to see the content that carries the meaning.

F.why: Erklärung is comfortable (~360px, 4–5 lines) and col 1 is a bit wider than D, but ~258px still forces ugly breaks with short tails: '…gesell/schaft', 'Bundesausbildungsförderung/sgesetz', 'Sicherheitsüberprüfungsgese/tz'. Readable, but the row-identifier column looks damaged.

reviews.unsure: A and C differ by only ~3px per column and look nearly identical; the ranking between them rests on 'Kfz-Haftpflicht' staying intact in C. Also, I cannot know whether horizontal scrolling (B/E) is tolerated in the target medium, which would change their verdict; and pixel widths are read by eye from the images.
